newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Lonrho in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Lonrho in merger talks.

text.p: British conglomerate Lonrho Plc and South Africa's JCI Ltd. said Monday they were discussing a merger in a deal that analysts said would create one of the world's largest mining companies.

The British conglomerate, whose activities range from mining to hotels to general trading, set out early last year to break up its sprawling empire. But it lost most of its luster as plans to split itself up were slow to materialise.
Lonrho has so far sold only one of its two hotel chains and disposed of Lonrho Sugar earlier this month. But it still has to spin off its African trading operations.

This would leave it with its extensive mining operations, which have now attracted the attention of JCI. Any merger with JCI might well coincide with the planned split of the South African trading businesses, analysts said.
A deal with JCI would make sense, adding a wealth of extra mining management expertise to Lonrho, said Charles Kernot at Paribas Capital Markets.

A JCI-Lonrho link also would offer a way out for major stakeholder Anglo American Corp. The European Union last month told Anglo to reduce its Lonrho stake to below 10 percent from its current 27.5 percent.

Kernot said Anglo could swap its stakes in both JCI and Lonrho for the latter's interest in Ashanti, the Ghanaian gold mining company. He estimated that 41 percent in Ashanti could be worth 540 million pounds ($885 million), while Anglo's combined holdings in Lonrho and JCI would be worth around 450 million pounds ($738 million).
"It would give the new entity complete independence ... and Anglo would get Ashanti, which is also something they would like," he said.
Other analysts said a JCI-Lonrho link-up was still far from a done deal, with other mining firms also interested in Lonrho's coal, platinum and gold activities.
"It (the negotiations) focuses attention on Lonrho being actually very cheap," said analyst Roger Chaplin at broker T. Hoare.

Analysts said it was likely Lonrho would consider teaming up with another company besides JCI. Market talk focused on South African firms such as Avmin Ltd. and Randgold Resources as possible alternatives.
"Lonrho would be doing shareholders a disservice by not taking other offers into consideration," said Kernot.
